ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are coordinate axes; the line y=x extends toward the upper right, and the line y=-x extends toward the lower right; the two intersect at the origin; on the right side there is the vertical line x=4. The base region enclosed by y=x, y=-x, and x=4 is a triangle, extending from x=0 to x=4. The figure also schematically shows a vertical slice perpendicular to the x-axis, whose corresponding cross-section is an equilateral triangle. Reasoning: For a fixed x, the upper end of the vertical slice in the base is at y=x, and the lower end is at y=-x, so the slice length is s(x)=x-(-x)=2x. Because the cross-section perpendicular to the x-axis is an equilateral triangle, its area is A(x)=(√3/4)s(x)^2=(√3/4)(2x)^2=√3 x^2. The volume is the integral of the cross-sectional area from x=0 to x=4: V=∫_0^4 √3 x^2 dx=√3[x^3/3]_0^4=64√3/3.

raw_record.question_text: The base of a solid is a region bounded by the lines $y = x$, $y = -x$, and $x = 4$. What is the volume of the solid if the cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis are equilateral triangles?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram to identify the base as the triangular region between y=x and y=-x from x=0 to x=4, and note the vertical slice shown is perpendicular to the x-axis. Use the text to confirm the cross sections are equilateral triangles. For a fixed x, the slice length is the vertical distance between the lines: s(x)=x-(-x)=2x. The area of each equilateral cross section is A(x)=(sqrt(3)/4)s(x)^2=(sqrt(3)/4)(2x)^2=sqrt(3)x^2. Integrate this area from x=0 to x=4: V=∫_0^4 sqrt(3)x^2 dx = sqrt(3)[x^3/3]_0^4 = 64sqrt(3)/3.

method.method_draft: Use the picture to view the base as a linearly expanding triangle from the origin to x=4. The text says the slices are equilateral triangles, so their side length equals the vertical width of the base at each x. Instead of subtracting the two line equations directly, use similarity/scaling in the triangle: the width is 0 at x=0 and 8 at x=4, so it grows proportionally as s(x)=2x. Then the equilateral cross-sectional area is A(x)=(sqrt(3)/4)(2x)^2=sqrt(3)x^2. Integrate over the full base interval shown in the diagram, 0≤x≤4, to get V=∫_0^4 sqrt(3)x^2 dx=64sqrt(3)/3.
